ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. run

4. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

5. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

6. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only a joining word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

8. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 9.4.1 Play: Style and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.5.1 Narrative compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Impromptu Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

3. D — run

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

7. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

9. B — Where is the library?

11. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 9.4.1 Play: Style; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 9.5.1 Narrative compositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Impromptu Speeches; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
